Release guide

Source: RELEASE.md

Not part of the built package (listed in .Rbuildignore). Version 1.0.1 has passed steps A to C on Linux. Steps D to F are done once the repository is public.

A. Prepare the source

  1. Update NEWS.md, the version in DESCRIPTION and CITATION.cff (version, date-released).
  2. Rebuild data if data-raw/ or the simulation engine changed: source("data-raw/datasets.R"), source("data-raw/wgh_targets.R"), source("data-raw/cdc_lms.R").
  3. Regenerate documentation: devtools::document(), and the README with rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd").
  4. Install the package (R CMD INSTALL .), then precompute the study vignettes: in vignettes/, run Rscript precompute.R. It knits each .Rmd.orig to .Rmd with figures in vignettes/figures/ and stops on any error. Read the knitted files and check that the prose still matches the numbers.
  5. Search the source for identifying names and study numbers, for example grep -rniE "paper [0-9]|<institution names>" R vignettes inst man README.md. Confirm that no real individual-level data and no model fitted to real data are included.

B. Three levels of evidence

Level What it shows How to run it CI
1. Package checks Installation, namespace, documentation, examples, unit and validation tests R CMD build . then R CMD check --as-cran WeGrowHealthR_x.y.z.tar.gz R-CMD-check.yaml, every push, Linux (devel, release, oldrel), Windows, macOS
2. Integration checks All 14 flows run end to end with models and outputs checked, SITAR recovery and selection, sequential against parallel equality NOT_CRAN=true WGH_INTEGRATION=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test()' with the package installed integration.yaml, weekly, on demand and on every v* tag, on the three systems
3. Environment checks Supported systems with all suggested packages (including learnr and targets), clean sessions The two workflows above install every suggested package on each system Both workflows

Also run all examples including \donttest: devtools::run_examples(run_donttest = TRUE).

Record the results of each level in the release notes. Levels 2 and 3 on Windows and macOS come from CI and cannot be shown on a single machine.

C. Build the release files

  1. R CMD build . gives WeGrowHealthR_x.y.z.tar.gz.

  2. Frozen Book 2 cohort: with the release installed, run

    library(WeGrowHealthR)
g <- wgh_simulate(30000, preset = "wgh_like", seed = 2026, style = "book2")$visits
saveRDS(g, "growdat2.rds", version = 3)
tools::md5sum("growdat2.rds")

    The file and its checksum are in the release bundle.

D. GitHub

  1. Create the public repository WeGrowHealthR and push the source (the contents of this folder, including .github/).

  2. Add the links to DESCRIPTION, either with usethis::use_github_links() or by hand:

    URL: https://github.com/nhanhocu/WeGrowHealthR, https://nhanhocu.github.io/WeGrowHealthR/
BugReports: https://github.com/nhanhocu/WeGrowHealthR/issues

    Add the same url to _pkgdown.yml and repository-code to CITATION.cff. Commit.

  3. Turn on GitHub Pages for the gh-pages branch (Settings, Pages). The pkgdown workflow fills it.

  4. Wait for R-CMD-check to pass on all five configurations and run the integration workflow by hand (Actions, integration, Run workflow).

  5. Create release v1.0.1 (tag v1.0.1), attach the tarball, growdat2.rds and growdat2.md5, and paste the 1.0.1 section of NEWS.md as the release notes.

  6. wgh_download() already points to https://github.com/nhanhocu/WeGrowHealthR/releases/download/v1.0.1/growdat2.rds with checksum 7e636199ba6d54c6de0b6cc94df40d05 (set in R/zzz.R). The asset name and the tag must match exactly. If the cohort is ever regenerated, upload it to a new release and update both values in R/zzz.R.

E. Zenodo archive and DOI

  1. Log in to Zenodo with GitHub and switch the repository on (GitHub integration page) before creating the release in D5. Zenodo then archives every release and reads CITATION.cff.
  2. After the archive appears, add its concept DOI to CITATION.cff (identifiers), to inst/CITATION and to the README, and use it in the software availability statement of the paper.

F. CRAN

  1. Check on the CRAN test services: devtools::check_win_devel(), devtools::check_mac_release() and rhub::rhub_check().
  2. Update cran-comments.md with the results.
  3. Submit with devtools::release() or the CRAN web form. Confirm the e-mail sent to the maintainer address.
  4. After acceptance, change the installation line in the README to install.packages("WeGrowHealthR") and tag the accepted version.

Points CRAN reviewers often raise, already handled: software names are in single quotes in DESCRIPTION, the reference has a DOI, examples that take more than a few seconds are in \donttest, tests that take long are skipped on CRAN, nothing is written outside tempdir() unless the user gives a path, functions with a seed argument restore the user’s random number state, and parallel workers are only used when the user sets a plan.
